children: U.S. equities pushed deeper into negative territory Thursday following Wednesday’s jump in Treasury yields.
The blue-chip Dow
was last -0.5%, the benchmark S&P 500 (
) was last -0.3%, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite
was last -0.6%.
Now, here are 4 news stories that broke in the morning to watch out for:
Treasury yields climb as 10-year reaches 5.15% on rate hike fears:
U.S. Treasury yields

their sharp rise Thursday, with the benchmark 10-year yield climbing 3.3 basis points to 5.15% and the 30-year yield gaining 4.1 basis points to 5.44%. The moves followed a selloff Wednesday that pushed the 10-year to its highest level since July 2007. Market pricing for an October Fed rate hike surged past 70% after St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said more rate increases were likely needed to quell inflation, citing strong demand and supply shocks including higher import and commodity prices.
GoDaddy jumps 14% following takeover approach from Gen Digital:
GoDaddy
shares

14% after reports that Gen Digital, maker of Norton 360 antivirus software, made a takeover offer in recent weeks. Gen Digital shares fell 7.6% on the news. Discussions remain at an early stage with no guarantee a deal will happen, according to the Financial Times. GoDaddy has a market cap of $12.2 billion, while Gen Digital is valued at $15.7 billion. Competitor Wix rose 6.5% in sympathy trading.
Oracle invokes force majeure on $18B New Mexico AI data center project:
Oracle

shares  fell after issuing a force majeure notice to Stack Infrastructure, the developer of the massive Project Jupiter data center in New Mexico. The notice seeks to shield Oracle from potential payments if the 2.45-gigawatt facility is delayed and does not come online as planned in 2028. The project is part of the broader Stargate artificial intelligence infrastructure effort involving Oracle, OpenAI, and SoftBank. About 20 banks provided an $18 billion loan to finance the campus. Blue Owl Capital shares fell 4%, Bloom Energy dropped 5%, and SoftBank shed 6%.
UPS forms first death cross since June 2023 amid price weakness:
United Parcel Service

formed a technical death cross for the first time since June 2023, with its 50-day moving average falling below its 200-day average near the $102–$105 range. UPS closed Wednesday at $95.82 after declining from above $110 in July. The previous death cross in June 2023 was followed by a 22% decline over the next five months. The stock carries a C momentum grade, with its six-month performance down 1.89% versus a 4.29% gain for the sector median, though its one-year return remains positive at 13.52%.
